utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Good morning, Ms. Galeva-Petrovska. Would you please stand, and if you would read aloud the affirmation on the card that is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mrs. Galeva. With your permission, I will address by just one of your family names. I will use Mrs. Galeva. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will also ask you to speak your answer into the microphone, because just nodding cannot be recorded in the transcript. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We have already met. You know that I am Edina Residovic, that I appear for Mr. Boskoski, and that I have a colleague in my Defence team, my co-counsel Mr. Mettraux. I am going to ask you, first, to tell the Trial Chamber your first and last names?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Sofija Galeva.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I start putting you any questions, I will kindly ask you to listen to another piece of information, or rather, instruction on my part. You understand the language that I speak, and I also understand the language that you speak. However, my question and your answer need to be translated so as to allow the Trial Chamber and my learned friends in the courtroom to understand both my question and your answer. Therefore, I would kindly ask you to wait for my question to be translated and only then start providing your answer. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please give us your birthday and tell us where you were born Mrs. Galeva?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: On the 20th of September -- I apologise. Should I start immediately or should I wait for everything to be translated into English? .

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can start answering and then I will wait for your answer to be translated, which means that you don't have to stop after every word. You can provide the full answer and then I will wait for the answer to be translated.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: On the 20th of September, 1970, in the city of Strumica in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about your educational background?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I have university education at faculty of the bar. I have passed the bar exam, and at the moment I'm enrolled in the post-graduate studies in the cathedral of international law diplomacy.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where you completed secondary education and then where you went to university?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I graduated from the secondary education in the city of Strumica and then I graduated from the faculty of law there Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Having graduated from the school of law in Skopje, where did you work? Can you tell us, briefly, something about your work history?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Immediately after I graduated from the faculty of law, I got employment in a private company as a lawyer, and I spent there a brief internal of time; and after that, I used to work as an attorney's apprentice in an attorney's office, again, in the city of Strumica, so that I have the necessary years of experience before I passed the bar exam.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When did you pass the bar exam; can you tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I passed the bar exam in 1996, I think it was February 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When somebody passes a bar exam in the Republic of Macedonia, what jobs can that person count on?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: The bar exam is a prerequisite for a person to be employed as a judge, as a prosecutor, as an attorney, as a legal representative of companies, et cetera. These are mainly the jobs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Galeva, what did you do after passing the bar exam?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: After I have passed the bar exam, I was again employed in a company. I was its legal representative. And, after some time, I also opened my attorney's office. I used to work as an independent attorney. That was somewhere in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you have your own firm and did it come the time when you changed both the place of residence and the place of work?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: In October 1998, I started my office, and I worked there until 2002, until I -- my employment in the Ministry of Interior. So I moved from Strumica to Skopje. So for some four years I had my office.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When did you joined Ministry of Interior, and when did you start working in Skopje at the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I remember that the job application procedure started somewhere towards the end of 2001, and I know that the first contacts with the Ministry of Interior were towards the end of December 2001; and after that, it was necessary to go through several months of formal procedure, which pertained to approvals and the securing funds from the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Macedonia for this job to be opened, which means that the procedure lasted several months. So I received my official employment contract for the Ministry of Interior on the 2nd of April, 2001 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, what was your initial position, when you signed the contract with the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: When the job contract with the ministry was signed, no specific job was defined in it. The rules provide that there is, first, a period of apprenticeship, which is the prerequisite to pass the professional exam and that, on the other hand, is the prerequisite to have a specific -- to be assigned to a specific job. So I started as an apprentice.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. On page 4, line 21 it says "April 2001," and as far as I could hear, it was "April 2002." Can the witness please confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you finally take the permanent job in the ministry in 2001 or 2002?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: 2002, 1st of April 2002 was when my job contract was signed. But from December 2001, the procedure of employment had started and I attended regularly - how could I put it? - regularly or from time to time, I was there in the ministry to follow the procedure to see how far the procedure went with regards to the securing the funds and, of course, to establish all contacts with the people that I would be working with, with my superiors at the job where I was to be assigned initially.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, the allocation of funds and the definition of your final job was completed towards the end of March and then you started going to work regularly every day on the 1st of April. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, when you first started working, what was your job? In what part of the Ministry of Interior did you work?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: As an apprentice, I was deployed at the sector of national bureau of Interpol that is within the police department within the public security bureau within the ministry. So this was my first post in this sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute ago you told us, Mrs. Galeva, that you had passed the bar exam which was a condition for the jobs that an expert in law might land. As far as I understand you, you started with an apprentice with the office of the Interpol in Macedonia. Was this -- was it necessary for you to pass any other exams in order to complement your previous education?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. And I have mentioned already that the prerequisite was to pass through this period of apprenticeship, then to satisfy the criteria for passing of the professional exam. If the superior officer for whom you're working within the apprenticeship gives an assessment that the person is capable, meets the criteria to pass this professional exam, and is able to further perform the professional tasks and duties independently, then the person is allowed to pass the professional exam. When passing the bar exam, you are meeting the prerequisite to have a formal employment contract for a specific job post for which specific tasks are envisaged within the description.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you pass the exam, and when was it?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. I passed the professional exam. That was towards the end of May 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And were you given a different title, or were you given a different position after that?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I remained for some two months in the sector for national bureau of Interpol; and from 1st of June 2002, I was deployed to a new job post. After I have passed this professional exam, I was given a specific job and title. That was state advisor within the cabinet of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Galeva, let's go back to that period while you still worked with the Interpol office. Tell me, what kind of tasks did you have in that department and upon whose proposal or request did you perform those tasks?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: While I was in this sector, considering that my status there was one of apprentice, our internal acts of the ministry indicate that during the performance of this apprenticeship, the apprentice must be introduced with many of the posts within that sector, and that under the systematicisation, the organisational structure belonged to that sector. The objective was to have the idea about the sector, what is the sector dealing with. With regards to the specific tasks, I went through several posts. I can speak in general what they were dealing with. That was the process of issuing warrants on persons, then the procedure of examining origin of cars that were imported from abroad. Those were the main tasks by that sector. There were additional ones, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did it ever happen that that you received a specific task that you were supposed to carry out while you were still an apprentice with the office of the Interpol?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I apologise. Are you referring to a specific task -- tasks related to the Interpol sector or outside of the domain comprised by the Interpol?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've just described the main tasks of the Interpol: The surveillance of persons, the inspection of vehicles, issuing warrant arrests and following them. What I would like to know is this: Did anybody at any point in time - and if they were, who it was - offered you or told you that you are supposed to do something else?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Well, since I started working in the Interpol officially from the 1st of April - I can't really remember the exact date, but that was towards mid-April - the head of the crime police department, Spasen Sofevski, invited me to his cabinet. We had some interview. He asked me generally whether I was informed that the process of exhumation of persons of -- corpse from Ljuboten was ongoing. He asked me what I had heard about this event, about this case. So we had a conversation around it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the under-secretary for the crime prevention police asked you this, what did he tell him? Had you heard anything about Ljuboten before that?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I had heard about it; but considering that was an event that took place before I was employed at the Ministry of Interior, I could not have had specific or detailed information about the events. My knowledge was mostly based on the information from the media newspapers. That was it. But I had heard of the event at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're saying that that interview may have taken place at mid-April, and the exhumation in the village of Ljuboten was taking place around that time. I would like to ask you whether the media, at the time, informed the population about the process of exhumation?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. On a daily basis, there would be news bulletins on the TV stations, the newspapers wrote about it, but those were superficial. I will use the colloquial term "superficial" information, because they themselves had no specific data about the way in which the procedure was carried out. So they informed, in general, that there was such process, that it was ongoing, what was its forecasted duration but no specific details were presented.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of that interview or conversation, did the under-secretary give you a task or an assignment; and from that moment on, did you have any close contact with the information that were -- that was heard with regard to the exhumation in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: During that conversation, he asked me about my prior work experience. He had already all information about my prior work experience, the jobs I had performed, and he stressed, having in mind that the fact that I had such experience appearing before the courts as an attorney, that it would be good for me to be involved in the procedure, not to participate in the process, but to follow it all the time. That was the time when that procedure of exhumation was carried out, April of 2002, and I, of course, accepted this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Galeva, before we go back to the assignments that you accepted and that were given to you by the under-secretary of the police, tell me, please, which department of the ministry incorporated the Interpol office where you worked as an apprentice pending the professional exam that you were supposed to pass?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I mentioned already that was the sector of the national bureau of Interpol within the criminalistic police department, within the public security bureau in the Ministry of Interior. And due to this, I suppose I was invited by the head of the crime police department, and he was the direct superior above the superior in the sector where I had performed my apprenticeship.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Galeva, before we go back to the relevant issue, I would kindly ask to you tell us briefly something about your further tasks that you were given in the Ministry of Interior. As a matter of fact, as far as I can remember, you have told me that on the 1st of June, you were appointed the -- a public official in the office of the minister as his associate.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. On the 1st of June 2002, I received my job contract for the position of state advisor within the cabinet of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, how long did you stay in that position?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: From the 1st of June, 2002, until the 1st of April, 2003.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout all that time, did you perform the same tasks in the office of the minister, or did there come a time that you had to interrupt that job and do something else?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Considering the fact that in September we had general elections, parliamentary elections, on the 1st of November, 2002, a new minister was appointed to the Ministry of Interior; and, of course, he established a new cabinet, and many shifts took place then among the employees. They were transferred from the present to new job positions, and I was among them, but I did not receive a contract immediately. The explanation was that they still hadn't found an adequate person who could perform that job; and for this reason, I was told that I should take my holiday leave and that I would be invited to be informed of what my new job position would be. And since that took quite a lot of time, I was, of course, rather eager to have this issue resolved and whatever happens happens. But I wanted my new contract, and I wanted to know what would be my new job and my new tasks in the future.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now tell us briefly whether you were assigned a new position and what tasks you performed later on in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: This lasted sometime until March of 2003. I was then invited by the new director for public security and the then state secretary in the ministry, and I was given my new job contract. So from the 1st of April 2003, I was already deployed to a new job that was a senior assistant on legal and personnel affairs within the department of legal, financial, and other affairs within the sector of internal affairs for the city of Skopje within the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any other duties besides the position that you were assigned in March 2003?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: During that time that was my main duty. I was working at that job.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And after?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: After that, I had a new job, but that was in 2005, in March, I believe. I believe it was the 25th of March, 2005, yes. This is when I received a new contract, and I was appointed head of the unit for legal, financial, and other common affairs within the sector for internal affairs, Skopje, within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you stayed there until this day or have you been assigned another job?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: No. I had a new contract afterwards. On the 3rd of July, 2007, I was appointed head of sector for misdemeanours within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what is your job at the moment?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, that's the same one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's go back to the part of your testimony where you told us that the under-secretary for the crime prevention police invited you to get involved in the Ljuboten case and to monitor the process of exhumation which was under way. On that occasion, did the under-secretary refer you to some other bodies? Did you know at the time who it was in the Ministry of Interior who was involved -- involved in the issues of exhumation?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. After the questions on how informed I was about those events, he then informed me, in general, about this event and about the process that was expected. That was actually ongoing, the process of exhumation; and, of course, the proposal came that I would be involved in this work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: And so he gave me the information that, initially, the Ministry of Interior was represented by the forensics police, the sector of forensics of the police within the ministry was the only representative of the ministry police. No other bodies were involved. And he suggested that it would be best to have -- for me to have the initial contact with the head of that sector, Miroslav Uslinkovski, since he was the most proper person who could give me the best information about all that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you contacted the crime technicians and Mr. Uslinkovski?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I made efforts to establish contact with Mr. Uslinkovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did he tell you at the time; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: That was our first meeting actually, the introductory meeting. I just informed him that I was authorised to monitor this process, but he was so busy, because at the moment the exhumation procedure was going on. So, later on, during that time and a bit later on, there were several occasions when we would meet, and he would inform me about some things related to the procedure. He would also give me some materials.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Galeva, having become an apprentice, having spoken to your immediate superior or other superiors, was there a time when you actually encountered or met up with Mr. -- Minister Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. There was such a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember when this happened, and what was the reason for you meeting up with him?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: This was around immediately somewhat a short period of time after I met with the head of the crime police, about the middle of the month of May, perhaps the end of the month, when I was again called by the head of the criminal police, and he told me to go to the office of the minister, that he is looking for me in regards to this case, which I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that it was not long after the under-secretary for the crime police tasked you with monitoring the exhumation process. Can you please be more precise in determining the period of time, the month or maybe even something more precise than that? The Trial Chamber would certainly appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I think this was the end of April 2002, the meeting with the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any other individuals in the minister's office at the time?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. The director of the bureau for public security, Goran Mitevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I move on to my next question, let me ask you this: You have already told us that at the time when you arrived that the under-secretary for the crime prevention police was Mr. Spasen Sofevski.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who at the time was the director of the state security?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Mr. Nikola Spasovski was the director of state security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you known when Mr. Spasovski had taken the position of the under-secretary?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact date, but I believe it was around August 2001, end of August 2001, but I'm not sure about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the director of the state security and minister having been present at that meeting. Do you remember whether you were told at the time why you had been asked -- do you remember the conversation with Minister Boskoski and Director Mitevski at the time at all?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. I recall that they were present there, those two persons, at the beginning when I came there. Later, and after the Director Mitevski presented me, he was told, among other things, about previous events that the head of the crime police charged me to follow the process of exhumation; and then the minister naturally asked me what I had undertaken in this regard so far, and they agreed what should be undertaken further with the director and what my concrete engagement would be in regards to this whole case. Then the minister proposed to the director that it would be well advised that I focus on this case, that I become fully engaged on this case. After the passing of the professional exam, it would be well advised that my new work position would be in the office of the minister where it was best -- the best position to follow this whole affair.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the conversation in the minister's office, which took place towards the end of April, as you've told us, did anybody mention anything to the effect of the ministry's organs having done anything prior to that?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. There was talk about this. I was immediately told that the Director Mitevski also worked in a commission charged exclusively for this event. Other members of the commission were also told to me, that they also possess materials which pertain to this case. I was told who else is engaged in this matter, and that there are other working groups, commissions, that were also charged to gather and to prepare certain materials.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were talking to the minister and the director, did anybody else join you at any point in time, or did the conversation end by only the three of you talking?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: After all of these things were said, the director explained to the minister, informed the minister, that, among the others who were included in this matter, there was a certain Katica Jovanovska, an analyst working in the sector of analysis and research at the ministry, who was charged to gather information to this period, somewhat before and somewhat after the event itself, from the 10th to the 12th of August, 2001, as well naturally the period of the conflict. Then the minister requested that she also be called in the office and that she be present during these talks so they can ask her how far she has gotten on this matter and how much information she was gathered in this area, in view of the task that she was charged with.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did this person join you? Were you introduced to this analyst who had worked on gathering information, as you put it, or compiling information with regard to Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. She was called immediately. She joined us in the office of the minister. She joined the discussions and informed about her work up until then. I recall that she informed about the fact that she has started preparing, in addition to others, an analyst report, a more comprehensive and complex information exclusively dealing with this event. She was charged to do this and that the preparation of this information was ongoing. She also informed that she has other material, and the minister and the director told her that all of these materials should be accrued in one place and handed over to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After this conversation in the minister's office, did you have other meetings with this lady, Katica, and did you receive from her any material? If you did, can you remember what kind of material that was?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Immediately, after the end of this conversation that took place in the office of the minister, I left and went to my office; and after some period of time, during the course of the same day, Katica came to my office with material which she handed over to me. As far as can I recall, this material included a number of analyst information, dealing with almost the whole period of the conflict. There were, of course, information about the Ljuboten event of the 12th of August; then material from Human Rights Watch with the recommendations to the government and accusations. Primarily, this is the material I received from her.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When she handed the material over to you, did you have any subsequent contacts with Mrs. Jovanovska?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, of course, because at this time she was working with an external associate on legal issues at the ministry. He had an office very close to mine, so she passed by here daily, as sometimes she brought in some information, sometimes she asked me the phase of the procedure and where it was at the moment and what was going done in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well, you told us that Mrs. Jovanovska had been in charge of compiling complete information about the events in Ljuboten. Did you ever receive this complete information that had been done on all the activities that had been carried out with regard to Ljuboten and surrounding Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: On one occasion she showed me the information, but this was not finalised. This was work in process. This was a text prepared on a computer, but there were a lot of hand-made notes on the text itself, and I recall that she told me the following: "Even if you read this, this is not easy to understand. I can't do it myself even. Wait a while and I will put it all in good order, and we will have all the necessary information that they expect of us." But soon after, she left the ministry and she became a judge. Afterwards, I contacted with the sector where me worked to track down and obtain this information. I recall I spoke with Vasilka, and I can't recall her last name. She was also a person higher up in the sector of analysis and research, and I told her all of this, that it is very important for me to obtain this information, but she simply explained that Katica by leaving and by the usual transfer and exchange that takes place when such changes were made, she had not handed any information over of this kind, nor did anyone employed there know anything about this. So we did not get this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I move on to a different topic, Your Honours, I would like to provide the witness, my learned friends, and the Trial Chamber with some documents that I would like to us in my further examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Galeva, your principle task, how did you understand it? Were you supposed to collect all the information? Were you supposed to analyse it? Were you supposed to write reports? Can you explain the way you understood the task that you had been given?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: My task was to collect the comprehensive material which the Ministry of Interior has, which pertains to the case of Ljuboten, without going into detailed analysis, preparing any kind of reports, strictly collection of material in one place; to prepare a chronology of these events; to put them in one place; and then to hand them over to the directors and to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did you set up -- or rather, how did you collect, how did you gather these documents that you had received?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Most often, there were personal contacts with individuals who at that time were, or prior to the event or when I took over this task, persons who were in leading positions who I believed could give me the best answers to the questions on which there were many dilemmas. These were conversations, oral conversations, which I carried out through contacts with these people. I received written material also on my request, of course, because primarily I established these contacts with the people who I thought could help me in this regard. I established a starting point on this, and then we agreed that on all subsequent information or related, we need not meet. Anything new that they would receive on this matter, they would send to me, be it by mail or through other means. The important thing was that I receive this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After your initial meeting with Mrs. Jovanovska joined you, when you received the material, and after having been transferred to the office of the minister on the 1st of June, tell me, did you have any other meetings with the minister? Did minister show any interest in what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Especially once I definitively transferred to the office of the minister, I focussed on this case in particular which was the most important thing at the moment. The minister called to see me, whether it be on the collegium, whether it be individual meetings. There were many such occasions, and it was evident that he was very much interested in having the information as soon as possible, because there were many speculations about there in the media. Throughout the public there was lots of speculation about this, and it was still not proved and it was not established, and it was difficult to hear all of this. That's why it was his interest to settle this matter as soon as possible. On each occasion that we met, he emphasised this: "Hurry up. Do as much as you can, as quickly as you can. Collect the material. Let not time elapse. We need to know the truth and what really happened there as soon as possible."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that he wanted to -- the truth to be known, can you please explain for the Trial Chamber, as he was asking for the truth to be revealed, did minister at any moment guided you towards the truth that you were to look for, or did he ask you to elucidate the whole thing and to gain the complete information, or whether there is a different, a third approach by the minister.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: In all of our meetings and in all of our discussions, he wanted an update of the procedure how much I had collected. I told him the people I had contacted, who I am with contact absolutely about everything that was going on, and he gave me absolutely support in this matter. As for special instructions, he let me know that a certain head of a sector of a unit could also give an answer to certain issues, so he gave me a kind of instructions, sort of to direct my activities, so I would not sway too much in this matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You've told us that Mrs. Jovanovksa handed over some of the materials to you containing reports by the Human Rights Watch and some information, as well as some analysis. Can you please try and recall how many pages of the information and analysis were contained in the file that was handed over to you by Mrs. Jovanovska?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the exact number. There was the report from Human Rights Watch; I recall this. And, as I said just a while back, there were analytical information, but I cannot tell you the exact number. They encompassed not only Ljuboten but a broader context, perhaps even the whole conflict period, although the focus was on the Ljuboten events. Due to these reasons, she as charged with the tasks to prepare this comprehensive information that would pertain particularly to this case. These were analytical information. I cannot tell you number, since this was the first day that she gave them to me. But it is not to be excluded that our-- in our pursuant meetings, she would give me a new piece of information, also analytical information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Galeva, I'm sure that at this moment, as you sit here, you cannot remember the total quantity of the information, but I would kindly ask you to look at the file that is before you and look at the document after tab 25, which is Exhibit 1D136. And, as we can see in the heading, this is a document issued by the Ministry of Interior, recorded under number 51, drafted on the 20th of August, 2001. Before I ask you anything about this document, obviously since you joined the ministry only in December 2001, would it be true if I said that at this time, the time of the document, you were not an employee of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: In August 2001, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the extent you can recollect the documents that you took over from Mrs. Jovanovska, could you please look at this information and tell me whether the file you had been given contained a piece of information with similar content; or maybe even this particular document, now that you're looking at this document, maybe you will be able to recall it. Did you have enough time to look at this document?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you then answer my question, and the question is this: Do you remember whether this document, whether this piece of information was among the documents that you received from Mrs. Jovanovska, or perhaps you cannot answer that question at all?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I believe I had this information in the file, which Ms. Jovanovska gave me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What has jogged your memory when you looked at document? How could you remember that this particular piece of information was contained in that file?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: It is -- it remains so in my memory. I remember the information which I received from her were prepared in such a fashion. There was a chronological order of events, a chronological approach to the events.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now kindly look at the document behind tab 26. The Exhibit number is 1D135 and the page is 1D1446 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's correction: 1D4416.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go immediately to page 2, which is 1D4417.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: My apologies. This is 26?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, 36 [as interpreted], tab 26?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Because I cannot see D 14. There's 1D35. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page, it's 1D00-4416. This is the first page. The other page is ... Do you have it now?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 1D4417, and you can see the number at the bottom of the page, in the upper portion, you can see that the number of the document is the same as the previous one. Even the date is the same, the date when the document was drafted. And now go back to the previous page, please, and the number of that page is 1D4416. We're looking at the bottom of the page. And now I would kindly ask you to tell me whether Mrs. Jovanovska or somebody else, for that matter, had ever explained to you why these documents had been drafted? Who needed that information and who were the people briefed about the information collected in that way?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I knew that those were information produced by the analytics department that were sent to the Minister of the Interior initially, and then they were forwarded to the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the file provided to you by Mrs. Jovanovska, do you remember whether this document or the letter that accompanied the original document was also there? The accompanying letter shows that this was sent to the government of the Republic of Macedonia to the attention of Mr. Ilija Filipovski. Can you remember whether in this file there were any similar documents reminding you of the one that you have before you at the moment?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I remember that the information I received through Katica were exclusively analytics information without such accompanying documents, to whom -- to whose attention is the information September; and whether it is the government or another institution, it was only analytical information elaborating on events that took place during that period. Now, whether those information were forwarded then to the government or another institution, I wouldn't know. And I am certain about this one, about this specific example, where it written that it is sent to the government of the Republic of Macedonia coordination body, crisis management body for the attention of Mr. Ilija Filipovski. I'm certain that there was nothing of the sort there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Can you please look at document after tab 27, which is Exhibit 1D34, and the page numbers are 1D1904. Please take some time to look at the document and then tell me whether, among the documents handed over to you by Mrs. Jovanovska, there was also this piece of information which was drafted in November 2001.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: As far as I remember, this information was included within the materials that I received from the director of public security bureau, Mr. Goran Mitevski, and not those that I received from Katica Jovanovska.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've now mentioned, again, director of the office of public security, Mr. Mitevski. As far as I can remember, at your first meeting with the minister, you also heard that a commission had already worked on these issues. Tell me, please, with regard to the tasks that you had been given, did you have any meetings with Director Mitevski; and if you did, what was the essence of your meetings? What did you discuss?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: With the director, Mr. Goran Mitevski, we met roughly several days after the meeting at the minister's office when he invited me in order to give me the materials that the committee had available. So it's the same issues that we already discussed in the meeting with the minister, because he was tasked with giving me a copy of all of the materials that the committee has gathered. And so I phoned him, I called him, we had a conversation, and he gave me voluminous written materials. We dealt with certain topics. We reviewed them document by document so that he could explain to me what was the nature of those documents, and he would give me guidelines for my future work, in terms of what they had done thus far and what could I contribute, what could I gather apart from those.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After quite a number of years that have passed, can you try and remember what was contained in the case file that Mr. Mitevski gave you?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, we had, first, the decision to establish the committee, minister's decision, the committee tasked with investigating the events of the 12th of August. I remember this decision was dated, I believe, afterwards. The 13th of August was the date when this committee was established. And its members were the director of public security bureau, Goran Mitevski, as the chair of the committee; then there were two members, General Risto Galevski, as the head of the police department, and Zivko Petrovski as Head of the Crime Police Department. That was a decision and it contained a provision that the committee is tasked with producing a report and information for the minister about those events. So this was -- there was this decision; then there was the result of this task, the information produced by the committee about the events in the village of Ljuboten; then there were many other materials, materials from the OSCE, some materials from the Ministry of Defence, from the army. There were also materials from the crisis management centre; also materials from the security and counter-intelligence directorate; then the department for internal affairs, Cair. Of course, there were also the materials on the exhumation, related to the exhumation; the proposal for the exhumation that was submitted by the ministry based on the minister's order submitted to the basic public prosecutor office and to the investigating judge. There was some additional things there; Official Notes, court acts, court requesting some information from the ministry as well. So those are the documents that can I remember at the moment. So it was a complex case file that really contained many documents within it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you sit here today, can you remember how many documents there were? At least give us an approximate number.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I can't give you any number. I can say that it was a voluminous file, but, really, I could not give you any number because I never counted them. It was very thick. It was a heavy case file, heavy to lift it, the materiels that he gave me and then those that I additionally collected.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you, Mrs. Galeva, to look at the document after tab 1, which is exhibit number P73. The first thing you told us was that from Director Mitevski you had received among the files of documents was a decision to establish a commission issued by the minister. You have before you a document dated the 13th of August, 2001. Do you recognise this document as the decision that Director Mitevski gave you?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've told us that the responsible directors of the ministry were the persons who were appointed to that commission. Their names are Mitevski, Galevski, and Petrovski. At the moment when you joined the Ministry of Interior in 2002, were these same people in the same positions? Did they perform the same documents?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Mr. Goran Mitevski, yes, he was the director of the bureau for public security. Mr. Risto Galevski, I believe he was no longer head of the department for police; or this is how I remember things, that he was at the police academy maybe, but don't hold me by my word. I know that he was no long negotiate this position. Zivko Petrovski was also no longer performing this position when I arrived at the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you try and remember, Mrs. Galeva, who were the people who replaced Galevski and Petrovski at the moment when you joined the ministry?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Head of the police department was Mr. Zoran Jovanovski, and head of the criminal police department was Mr. Spasen Sofevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please look at document which is after tab 2 in my binder. This is Exhibit number P378. In answering my previous question, you said that in the case file that you had been given at the time, there was also a piece of information that the task force compiled in keeping with a decision and the task given to it. When you look at this information that is before you now, would you say that this is the document that was handed over to you by Director Mitevski in his case file?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, that is the information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've also told us that the case file contained certain other documents. You've told us that there were the UBK documents. Before I go on showing you some other documents, can you please tell me whether you actually read all the documents that you had been given by the director?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: From the director of the public security bureau, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: There were some information, yes, coming from the UBK directorate for security and counter-intelligence. Of course, I had read those. I had started those.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you able to recall what the information was all about? Did it have anything to do with the task that you were given.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. Those were information received again during that time dealing with this entire period. There was an information. I remember one rather more comprehensive information that made an overview when the -- a bit also to the period before it, but it was focussed on the events of Ljuboten and it was rather interesting as the other information, the shorter information, because they presented interesting materials. Those were materials refuting the assertions that on the critical date civilians were injured, that there were crimes against civilians, et cetera. The information gathered by the administration speak to something completely different. They are based on the information from the field, from the surveillance and operational technologies, as well as other methods, that are dealing with this entire period. And it was known in advance, or maybe I shouldn't use the words in advance, but during all time, it was known what was under preparation and what was about to happen there in that area. There also information from the interviews from the -- from the conversation with the informants people who were giving them information about the developments, related to logistical support, strategy, mode of operation, what is being done. Some names were also mentioned, the people involved in that, and under whose command things were done during the event?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at the document after tab 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Exhibit 1D141. Page 1 is 1D4707 in the English version and 1D4705 in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've just told us, Mrs. Galeva, that the case filed contained a lot of information. If you can't recall clearly whether you saw this information, I'm not going to insist; but if you can remember, then please tell us if you ever saw this piece of information, i.e., whether this piece of information was of the nature similar to the documents that you saw in the director's case file, the one he handed over to you. Please try and answer my question.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I can't say with certainty, but I know that there were numerous similar information. I can't really be absolutely certain when reading these names here or something, but I know there was similar information, many of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am now going to ask to you lock at the document which is behind tab 7, the following tab.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: 7, do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise. Actually, it is the document after tab 7 which is 1D142. Yes, I was right the first time, and my question is the same as the previous one. First of all, can you remember whether this piece of information was contained in the case file that you had been given, i.e., whether this type of information was something that was contained in the case file that you received from Director Mitevski?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: There were numerous such information. There were similar information in the material that I received from Mr. Goran Mitevski, as well as in the materials I received from Mr. Nikola Spasovski, since the -- as a director of the directorate for security and counter-intelligence, of course he offered me many such documents, information gathered, interviews carried out. There was a large number of those.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that the -- this would be a good time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will have the first break now and resume in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Galeva, before I proceed with my questions, I'd like to inform you that during the break, I had a look at the transcript and now I would like to clarify one thing with you. That maybe the result of either the interpretation or the result of my question put in a concern way. I would kindly ask you to answer this: If you remember, you've told us that, in December, you started looking for a new job. Tell me, when exactly did you sign your first contract with the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Work contract was signed the 1st of April, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And before that, did you have a contract of any kind? As I could see here, you said that you had something that implied a procedure.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: This was the end of December 2001, if I'm not mistaken, 25th of December, 2001, when I was called in for the first time and was told that there was an empty work position in this sector and that we can start the procedure to -- for my employment. This was, I believe, the 25th of December, 2001; then the formal procedure was carried out of approval, securing resources. But throughout this whole time, I was almost always present in the ministry. I came earlier, this is true, prior to concluding the first contract in order to acquaint myself with the work that I will be doing with my direct superiors and those above them to see how the structure and the organisational positioning of the ministry was. These were contacts with the sector for legal and general affairs and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that this now clarifies the answer that you provided earlier on page 4, line 20, and page 5. However, I would ask you this: After having signed your first work contract on the 25th of December, during the period of time which started with the 25th of December until the moment you finally took the job on the 1st of April, did you come to the ministry, and during that period of time, did you perform some tasks in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. Almost throughout this whole time, I was present there with some breaks naturally. Since my law firm was still operational, it was not closed down. I came here. As I said, I carry out the regular context I mentioned, with the persons I mentioned, with whom I had to work later on. I went to the places where I had to spend my period of apprenticeship, which preceded the conclusion of the second work contract; that is to say, the decision of the 1st of April, 2002, continually. From the period from 25th of December - if the date is correct - 2001, to obtaining the contract in April 2002, I was present in the ministry with small breaks in between. And, in a way, I was included in the work that preceded it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now it's a bit more clear to me. When you were talking about having received documents from Director Mitevski, you've told us that the case file also contained some documents from other sources and other organs of the Ministry of Interior. As far as I can remember, you mentioned some documents that originated from Cair. Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please look at the document behind tab 3, which is P46.16. Did you ever - and when - see this document?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I have seen this document. I believe it was part of the material which I received from Director Goran Mitevski in -- and the material I received from Petre Stojanovski who was assistant of criminal police in the sector of interior affairs for the city of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please look at the document which is after tab 4 -- I apologise, tab 5, and the exhibit number is P23.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document is under seal, I suppose because of the fact that it has been shown to somebody whose identity may be revealed through this document. That is why I would ask for the document not to be shown in public.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As we can see, this document originates from the police station in Mirkovci, at Cair, and it's an Official Note. Please look at this document and tell me whether you saw this document before; and if you did, on what occasion and when you saw it. Did you see it in the case file provided to you by the director or on some other occasion and in some other place?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I'm sure that this was part of the material I received from Mr. Petre Stojanovski, but it is not to be excluded that it was also part of the material of Goran Mitevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can tell, it's on the screen that document P46.15 appears. This is the previous document that I asked the witness about. This document is after tab 4, and is also under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now can you see it on your screen. And since we already have the document on the screen, I'm going to ask you whether you ever saw this document before and also on what occasion and in what place; obviously, if you did see it at all.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. I have seen this document as a document prepared by the sector of the crime lab, the forensics, at the request of the investigative unit of Basic Court Skopje II, where they request supplemental answers to certain questions. As for exactly which material this was a part of, perhaps this was part of the two materials I mentioned, and it is possible that I received this from the sector of the forensics, the materials I received from there, because this is this document, after all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now we will go back to the document after tab 5, which is also a document under seal. The Exhibit number is P23. As far as I can remember, you have already told us that you saw this document before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is in line 9, and you told -- you've told us this is an Official Note; this is in line 10. I asked you about it, and you say in line 15 that you're sure that you received this material from Petre Stojanovski, but you cannot rule out the possibility that it is part of the Goran Mitevski case file. Would that be your answer with regard to this document?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In answering some of my previous questions, as far as I can remember, you've told us that the materials that you received also contained a conclusion of the government which had considered the information by the first commission. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. This material included a government conclusion which charged the Ministry of Interior and the Ministry of Defence to prepare a joint information for the events in Ljuboten; that is to say, there was an obligation for both ministries to that end.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the document after tab 10. This is Exhibit number 1D134. Mrs. Galeva, tell me, please, did you ever see this document before?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: The conclusion of the government, I have seen, but not in this form and shape. The content is the same. The form is different, however.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what was the form of the conclusion that you received from Mr. Mitevski? What did it look like?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: It was a text written in the usual way, on a piece of paper in written form, not in this form in which it is given here, with tables. A typical conclusion passed by the government, an ordinary written text.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I thank you. In answering my previous question and providing some explanation, you have told us that in that material, and in the government's conclusion, there was also an obligation on the part of the Ministry of Interior and the Ministry of Defence to draft some additional documents. Is that what you've told us?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. There was a -- the government charged the two ministries to prepare a joint information that will deal exclusively with this event.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see any documents that would mean that the government's conclusion had been carried out?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Well, yes. As far as I can recall, this was at the beginning of September 2001. This was the date of the conclusion of the government. So, by the end of the month, the information was prepared by the Ministry of Interior, and a proposal was given to the Ministry of Defence. Through the state secretary, a joint meeting was requested, on which this can be -- this could be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now kindly ask to you look at the document after tab 11, which is Exhibit number 1D137. Tell us, please, whether this document is the one that you have just testified about.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can see, this is the information. This is the address of the state secretary of the MOI, Buckovski, to the Ministry of Defence with a proposal for the proposal of the information be amended and finalised on this joint meeting that he is requesting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any material that would provide you with information as to what had happened later with the proposal for joint information to be drafted?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I know that this was the position of the government and that this joint information had to be drafted and prepared. What happened after that, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Besides the meeting with Mr. Mitevski when he provided you with all this information and some of the documents, when it came to the tasks with the same regard, did you continue meeting with Mr. Mitevski; and if the answer is yes, what was the goal of these meetings and what did you talk about during those meetings?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, there were such meetings in continuity. Surely, he was interested in what I do and what I was doing, which materials I was collecting; and on each such occasion and meeting, he gave me additional information, not just in written form but also verbally -- verbal information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you provided an overview of all of the informations that was initially given to you by Mr. Mitevski, you mentioned that there was also a proposal for exhumation. Can you please explain and tell us what this was all about?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Concretely, on this proposal, it is true that I spoke about this with Director Goran Mitevski, and he explained to me everything that transpired and preceded the proposal for exhumation. This critical day, to call it such, of the 12th of August, information was given by the MOI through the duty operations centre. The investigator submitted to the duty investigative judge and public prosecutor about what had happened. But in view of the truly serious security situation of that day, it was practically impossible to go there to that place. An attempt to that extend was made two days later, on the 14th of August, when a team was formed with an investigative judge, deputy public prosecutor, a doctor, expert persons from the forensic unit at the ministry who came to the unit to OVR Cair. He had a meeting with the head of OVR Cair, Ljube Krstevski, and the goal was this: Such a team to investigate was formed, the goal of which was to go to the site of the events. At that moment, they are in contact and establish cooperation with member of parliament -- Fatmir Etemi, member of parliament, who for the most part, because he was already on the in the village, had to inform them about the situation there and the possibility for that investigation team to go there and complete its task. Therefore, they made a number of attempts, but they were unsuccessful due to the fact that the security situation did not allow this. This is why it was subsequently decided that this be done in some future time, when the international community was also expected to take part and to secure the conditions to carry out this exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. I'm just wondering whether it could be clarified whether this lengthy explanation that the witness has just given was information given to her by Goran Mitevski, information that she compiled and analysed from all of her sources, or what is her source for this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Galeva, you have heard the objection and the Prosecutor's question. The Prosecutor would like to know whether you heard all this from Goran Mitevski or whether you obtained some of this information through your own analysis of the materials?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: This was first as information given to me by Director Goran Mitevski; but the same information, I also received from other sources, from employees at the ministry, and I think that follows throughout for the whole material. This event and the activities undertaking -- undertaken by the MOI, which was not made possible, was part of these materials.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now that we have just mentioned this exhumation proposal and you said that it was first mentioned to you by Director Mitevski, did he ever tell I who it was that submitted this exhumation proposal?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. The proposal was given by the Minister of the Interior. This was the beginning of September 2002 -- 2001, and it was submitted to the basic public prosecutor's office and to the investigative judge at the investigation unit at Basic Court Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now kindly look at the document behind tab 13, which is P102. Tell me, please, when it comes to this document, was it contained among the documents that you received from Goran Mitevski or did you receive this document in some other way, through some other channels?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I received this from Mr. Goran Mitevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the very top of this document, you can see some corrections. At the time when you received the document, did you notice these corrections in the left upper corner?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. I noted this immediately, and I asked about this. I was allowed to see a supplement document which came together with this proposal submitted to the basic public prosecutor's office and the duty investigative judge, where it is said that this is a technical mistake. Since there was only a technical mistake of the month, there was a supplemental document to that end stating this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please look at the document after tab 15. But before that, if we you look at that document, could you please tell me whether, while performing the task that you had been given, whether you also learned that the prosecutor's office, i.e., the court, accepted the initiative on the part of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. This is document from the public prosecutor's office to an investigative judge from the Basic Court. I have not seen this document. I have not seen this document, but I was told that immediately after the submissions of the proposal of the 7th of September, 2001 for the exhumation from the minister of the ministry, the same was accepted by the basic public prosecutor's office, which then submitted a proposal for undertaking various investigative activities to the investigative judge. Thus, the proposal was accepted. This is what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you properly, in the documents that were handed over to you by Mr. Mitevski, there was no document to this effect, i.e., this document was not contained in that case file. Please answer because I believe that your answer has not been recorded. Your answer to my question has not been recorded. Please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I have not seen it, but I was told; and afterwards in the material related to this area, it was noted that such document existed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was Exhibit number P55.02. We have just looked at that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now I'm going to ask to you look at the document after tab 16, which is P -- Exhibit 1D46. The Exhibit number is 1D46. This is an Official Note by the investigating judge, Dragan Nikolovski. Tell me, please, whether you received this document from Mr. Mitevski?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I had received this document because this was a document, act, sent to the ministry, more precisely to the public security bureau, and they requested some additional information, some data, to be elucidated before the process of exhumation were to start. As you can see, those data pertain to the identity of the buried people, the location of the graves, time of burial, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could we now please look at the document after tab 18, which is exhibit 1D47. Tab 18, 1D47. As can you see, this is another document by the investigating judge, Dragan Nikolovski. Tell me, did you ever see it before; and if you did, when was it that you saw it?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I have received this document from the director, Mr. Goran Mitevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I can then take it that you received this document among all the others that were provided to you by Director Mitevski?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please look at the document after tab 17, which is exhibit 1D73.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The page number is N005-0754 in the Macedonian version, and we also have an English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Galeva, we have before us a document by the Ministry of Interior bearing the date of 18 September 2001, and it is entitled "Official Note." Mrs. Galeva, tell me, please, at the time when you were charged with the relevant tasks, did you see this document; and if you did, can you remember who it was that had provided it to you?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I remember that this was an Official Note produced by the criminal police and I believe it was given to me by the head of the forensics, Mr. Miroslav Uslinkovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you spoke to your superiors, Director Mitevski, and the minister, and when you briefed them on what you were involved with, tell me, how did you understand the whole situation? Did you understand that the police work was something that was very much confined to the framework of the police, or was it rather a transparent activity with regard to the investigation of this problem?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: From everything that I collected, all the materials, all the interviews I conducted, I gathered the impression that the work was completely transparent; nothing was hidden. From the very beginning of the work, all justice system bodies were involved. The judiciary, the public prosecutor's office, and the government was informed about all of that. So everything that took part within the ministry was communicated to the outside. Nothing was hidden. Everything was transparent, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you had received this Official Note, and I suppose that you read it and learned about it its contents, but can you confirm: Did you read this Official Note?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. I remember this Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to look at the last paragraph in the Macedonian language on page 1, which also the last paragraph in the English version, again, on the first page. I'm go to read it to. It says here: Dr. Aleksej Duma affirmed his willingness to affect the exhumation and autopsy following the previously served order from the investigating judge; and also stated that in order to avoid any subsequent manipulation of the autopsy results of the buried remains in the village of Ljuboten, he would arrange for his supervisors to be present during the investigation, in the form of competent individuals from the Skopje office of The Hague Tribunal." In this regard, I would like to ask you, Mrs. Galeva, whether, through your conversations with Director Mitevski and other superiors and heads of departments, you could gain a certain understanding of the workings of the ministry. Was the ministry open to provide all information and to involve the international community in clarifying all the issues surrounding the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. So that was their attitude, attitude of the ministry, first of all; and then it was reiterated in the consultation meeting that preceded the procedure of exhumation, where a joint position was taken that the best option would be to allow for the participation in the procedure of the supervisors from the ICTY office in Skopje in order to avoid any manipulations. And at that, the forensics police or any other services from within the ministry would be made completely available for any needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go back to something that you said at the very beginning. After your first meeting with the under-secretary for crime prevention police, at which he asked you to follow the exhumation, as far as I can remember, you said that you spoke to Mr. Uslinkovski first and that he also confirmed to you that the forensic technicians were in the process of exhumation, but that at the time they were engaged and they could not brief you any further. Tell me, after that, did you have any other contacts with Mr. Uslinkovski?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I had several meetings with him. I met him several times, both meetings between the two of us and group meetings. So he informed me on absolutely everything on the entire course of the exhumation procedure, and he provided some interesting findings from this. Initially, that allegedly the entire procedure was headed by an investigating judge from our judicial bodies, while the main leader was the representative of the ICTY, the investigator Tucker, and the pathologist Eric, and that the forensics police was basically -- of the Ministry of Interior was basically just a technical service to provide all the facilities for the operation to be carried out. Apart from this - if this what you were referring to - after the procedure of exhumation was completed what was I told from Uslinkovski, we had very interesting discussions regarding this. Actually, that was the main purpose. The exhumation was to provide answers to many questions, many dilemmas presented at that time, and this is why it was of utmost importance to complete everything as soon as possible and to provide the answer.
