However, it was impossible to publish the answer because the MOI was in charge only of making an Official Note about the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Let me ask you something else. In addition to the number of conversations that you had with Mr. Uslinkovski, as you have just told us, did you receive from him any materials given the task that you had been given? Did Mr. Uslinkovski, i.e., the forensic technicians, give you any documents with regard to the exhumations that they were involved in?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I received the Official Note produced by them. I received some sketches, maps of the locations of the graveyards, places where the persons were buried, some photo albums containing photographs of those persons. Mainly, that was the range of the materials.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now please look at the document after tab 19, which is Exhibit number P55.34. Mrs. Galeva, did you ever see this document before? Was it provided to you with the other documents from some body?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. This was a list of persons, individuals from the forensic police that participated in this procedure. I received a copy of this document, again, from the head of police forensics sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please look at the document after tab 20, which is Exhibit number 1D05.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first page in the Macedonian version bears the number - I apologise - N001-0130; and in the English version, it is 1D00-2923.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a report on the exhumations conducted in Ljuboten drafted by the Basic Court in Skopje; the Lower Court II in Skopje, that is. Before we start dealing with the document, tell me, please, Mrs. Galeva, whether you saw the document before?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I haven't seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now can you look at the document after tab 21, which is Exhibit number 1D74. Also, before we actually start discussing the document, can you tell me whether you ever saw this document before?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now can we look at the document which is after your tab number 23, which is Exhibit number P55.20.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first page number in English is ET N002-1196 to N002-1207.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see this document? Did you receive its copy as part of your task that you had been given?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. I received this document from the sector for forensics police. I had received a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, when you look at this document, what does it contain?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: This document deals with the entire process of exhumation and post-mortem.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, I apologise. You started by saying that Mr. Uslinkovski provided you with some interesting information with regard to the exhumations and post-mortems. Tell me, if you remember, of course, what would the most important things that you found most intriguing with regard to the impression that was shared with you by the head of the crime prevention and forensic department who assisted the exhumations?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: This is the Official Note that actually deals with the formal procedure exhumation and post-mortem. And about the results now? The results need to be officially produced by the Forensics Medicine Institute, who was tasked with that; and before that, one couldn't say anything. The judge can't say anything, nor the institute. But one could not preclude the possibility -- actually, in an informal conversation, I was told those interesting things that I had mentioned. First, I heard them in conversation with Mr. Uslinkovski. I was asking the question about what could one see there, because there was a post-mortem performed on those ten corpses, and certainly some findings from that could serve as indicators and speak to something that could later provide some clarification. His general idea was that, and also what he said was, that at no rate - and he expressly stated this - it was completely impossible that they were civilians with the exception of three persons: That young boy, the 13-year-old boy; then the older man who died of cardiac arrest. Because for the two persons, so with the exception of this heart attack person, it was definitely established that they were hit by shells, and we know that this was not within the armament of the Ministry of Interior. Secondly, for the remaining individuals, it was very interesting that in August, for instance, when we know what is the climate in Macedonia, the high temperatures, and they were all wearing - most of them - wearing black jackets, thick woolen socks, and sweaters. On some of them bullets were found. So they were wearing black T-shirts or camouflage T-shirts. So all of that were indicators that deviated from the topic of or from the thesis that those were civilians only. And I will stress, again, the head of the forensics police on the basis of what he saw, because he was the most active participant, was the only one from within the ministry who was a participant. So his final position was that it was absolutely impossible that those were civilians. But I mentioned this before as well. Still the ministry was in a way left aside during this process. Its only role was to be the technical service, while the final word belonged to the ICTY investigate, and it was all chaired by the judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Given the fact that you embarked on this job in order to monitor the process of exhumations and post-mortems as a precondition towards finding out what had happened, tell me, did you have any meetings with some other individuals from whom you wanted to obtain either information or documents?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Regarding the exhumation, yes. So, since it was already ongoing, this was towards the end of the exhumation, I asked for a meeting with Mr. Duma, the director of the Forensics Medicine Institute. Immediately After the discussion with Mr. Uslinkovski, I believe he would be able to provide some answers to questions. In the conversation with him, I got the answer that he could not give any official information, because the legal obligations determined that the entire flow of the information that the reports that the Forensics Medicine Institute needs to produce should be submitted officially to the Court and not to the Ministry of Interior, and that was why he was not able to give me any written information. But we did have an oral conversation which was also very interesting, because it was to, a large extent, identical to what I had already heard by Mr. Uslinkovski. Those same notions were confirmed that Mr. Duma, that all the metal fragments found inside the persons' bodies were part of a projectiles of the shells and that the shelling was done from a distance. This gives strong evidence to the fact that there were discrepancies between the notions of weapons that the Ministry of Interior had. These are convention weapons, recognised weapons. I should not enumerated, but there is a rule book dealing with this; handguns, automatic guns. So shelling was outside of the possibilities of the Ministry of Interior, as well as other items found there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mrs. Galeva, did you have just one meeting with Professor Duma or did you have several conversations with him dealing with that topic?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Initially, I had one meeting. The first meeting was during the exhumation, but he was very busy as everybody else. And we, of course, agreed for the exhumation procedure to be completed; and after that, we had several meetings. But those were oral meetings, one-on-one meetings, when all the issues were presented to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that Professor Duma had told that you he would send all the post-mortem reports to the investigating judge, because this was the only legal requirement upon him and the only legal possibility for him to give a post-mortem reports to anybody. My question is this: In your conversation with him, did you learn from him whether, in the course of the exhumations, any other expertise had been requested; and if the answer is yes, do you know who the experts were who performed those expertise?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I apologise. Could you please repeat this question about the expert testimony, expertise?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, Mr. Uslinkovski had told that you he was involved in the technical side of the exhumations. He referred you, in a certain way, to Professor Duma. Professor Duma, if I understood you correctly again, told you that he had to draft the post-mortem reports and that the only person he could give them to was the investigating judge who was in charge of the whole case. However, you also told me that Professor Duma confirmed what Uslinkovski had told you, and that is that some fragments of weapons had been found as well as some other things. What I would like to know from you is this: In your conversations either with Uslinkovski or with Duma, was reference made to any other forensic expertise was carried out in addition to post-mortems; and if you were told anything to that effect, do you know who the experts forensics experts were? Who was it who should have been in charge of those things? Was it the Ministry of Interior? If that was never mentioned, obviously you cannot answer my question, but my question is whether you remember anything of that sort was ever mentioned in your conversations.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. Those issues were mentioned among other issues. It was mentioned that -- that despite the request that our bodies participate in the expertise on the findings, still, the representatives of the supervisors of the ICTY office in Skopje insisted that they exclusively participant in the expertise, that the expertise will be carried out in some independent laboratory in Netherlands. After that, during a subsequent meeting that I had with the judge as well, I learned that, allegedly, the investigator made a promise that a complete report from the NLA [as interpreted] analysis, a comparison with the family members and the overall expertise of the ballistic materials that were taken to the independent laboratory, that the entire report will be submitted to our court as well, but this did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I believe that you have just mentioned that at one point in time you had a meeting with the judge. Did I understand you properly? Did I understand you well; and if I did, could you then please tell me who is it that you met with and what did you discuss?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And before that, in line 21, page 50, there is a mistake in the transcript. It says here that a report is expected from the "NLA." However, the witness said that the report in question is a "DNA" analysis report.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I asked you something and then I interrupted you before the page moved forward to correct a mistake in the transcript. Let me repeat. If I understood you correctly, you have just told us that this was told to you by a judge in one of your meetings. Now I would like to learn, hear from you whether you met with any judges; and if you did, who that person was and what was discussed?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Immediately after that, I had a meeting with the investigating judge, Dragan Nikolovski, the judge who was in charge of the entire process. He was in charge, together with another colleague, Beqir Shaqiri. I had a meeting only with the first investigating judge, and I also obtained similar data from him. I asked him for some materials in writing, and I received the same answer, that he excepts that the Forensics Medicine Institute report will be submitted, but the law provides this they not communicate that to the Ministry of Interior. After the judge receives it, the judge should finalise the case file, and then send that to the ICTY. He also mentioned the expertise and it was the same story, that the expertise was not permitted here by our bodies, not even with the presence and participation of the representatives from the ICTY, and that this will be carried out in that independent laboratory. However, our court never received any report from that; neither related to the DNA analysis nor the expertise on other ballistic materials.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you have just mentioned something to that effect, can you remember how much after the exhumation did you meet with Judge Nikolovski?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I cannot say precisely, but it was during the summer, June/July, that's for sure, but I cannot recall the exact date. But it was around this time. The process itself lasted until the end of April and then afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mrs. Galeva, in addition to the persons who were in one way or another involved in the exhumations and with some of you -- some of them you had certain conversations only and from some of them you received certain documents as well, you have also mentioned that you were provided with some sketches and photos. Can you please look at the document after tab 24, which is Exhibit number P49.098.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, we have only the Macedonian version on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'll kindly ask to you look at the second page of this document and read what it says on that page. As you can see, there is a stamp in the upper part. Can you please read what it says here. Do you want me to read or are you going to read what is says in the circle in the stamp?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: "MOI, forensic unit, criminalistic techniques."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: "Sketch from on-site investigation case one, referring to Muslim grave sites in village of Ljuboten, where exhumation will be -- of ten grave sites will be carried out."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please go to the next page. Again, you see the sign of the forensic laboratory and the sketch of the site. My question is simple: You said that you had received certain sketches. Is this one of them, or did you receive some similar sketches from the forensic technicians of the Ministry of Interior who provided you with all the materials with regard to the exhumations?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: There were -- there was there sketch but also there were others. This was not the only one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In addition to the person who is were in one way or another involved in the process of exhumations, tell me, from the moment you took over the task, did you have any contacts with persons and bodies within the Ministry of Interior who could have provided you certain information? Let me ask you this: Did you ever have any contact with Mr. Zoran Jovanovski of whom you said that he was the under-secretary for the police in the public security bureau?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovski, yes. Did you ask him and could he provide any information?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I had a conversation with him. I was interested to confirm the rumours of involvement of police forces in this event; however, he told me that this could be best answered by General Galevski. Also, I was interested to know was in view of the fact that he was president of the commission about the accusation on the part of the Albanians for maltreatment. He said that he had received no application where they accused policemen for having maltreated them. Since I had already spoken to General Galevski, before seeing Jovanovski, I asked, subquestions, if you will, and identical answers were given to that given by General Galevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Outside of the ministry at the state level, did you establish any contacts with some other persons in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Outside the ministry?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the leadership of the Republic of Macedonia. Did you find any sectors, departments, where you could communicate with certain persons; and if you did, could you please tell us who they were.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: In addition to the persons already mentioned, I had -- I was in communication with the bureau for security and counter-intelligence. I had a conversation with General Galevski on numerous occasions; with operative technique units; with Petre Stojanovski, assistant of forensics of -- at the OVR Skopje; operative technical unit. I spoke with --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's take things one at a time in order not to confuse the whole matter. You have told us that were in communication with Petre Stojanovski who was the assistant minister for crime police in the security sector of Skopje. Could you perhaps remember who it was and who put you in contact with Mr. Petre Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: It was at the beginning, when I was charged with the task about this event, and my meeting with Katica Jovanovska, who in fact arranged the first meeting and the first talks with Petre Stojanovski, assistant of criminal police at the sector for internal affairs, Skopje. This was our first such meeting, where Jovanovska was also present. He was informed, in short, what my tasks were and what I was working on; and in my discussions with him, he told me that he has a particular interest, that he inducing particular efforts to come to information to find out whether members of the police forces did, in effect, take part in these events; and if this was so, to establish who they were, to establish their identity so that adequate measures can be taken. Efforts were put in, in particular with OVR Cair, since this is the regional sector, and this is where all of the events transpired. So he was in direct link with OVR, with the head of the OVR Cair. But on numerous occasion, he said that on-site visits were made, under very dire security situation; nonetheless, our operatives go there in order to investigate this. Many efforts were made to establish contacts with the Albanian population.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's take things slowly, please. Let's go back to certain things. Let's go back to your first meeting with Petre Stojanovski, which took place together with Katica Jovanovska who had actually taken you to him and introduced you to him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After that, did you have any other meetings with Mr. Petre Stojanovski? Did you discuss all the issues that you just started talking about? Where did these meetings take place? How were they organised?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: As I mentioned, this was our first meeting, during which Katica was also present. Later on, we met also. We had individual meetings, either in my or his office. He sometimes gave me materials during these meetings, or he sent them by mail, by regular mail. Therefore, I had a number of meetings with him where we talked about a lot of issues, and we agreed about a lot of issues that were pertinent to the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that he provided you with a lot of materials, and my question is this: When you saw him the first time thereafter or some other time, did you ask for these materials from him, or did he provide these materials to you spontaneously? Did Mr. Stojanovski provide materials to you without having to ask? Actually, was this the first time ever that he sent any such materials to the Ministry of Interior, or was that a previously established practice?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I recalled he said that I was not the only one coming to him requesting such information and material. People before me, my colleagues, requested such materials, similar materials pertaining to this case. And he said, since I was there, he wanted to know how he could help. He had offered some materials he had at his disposal and promised that everything that would ensue in the process of work he would then send to me as well..

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then, if I understand you well, he provided some of these materials to you personally and the rest he sent by internal mail?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Regular mail, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he ever tell you whether the police of Skopje had been involved in the exhumations? Did you ever discuss any such thing?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: He told me that he is updated, that -- and knows of this process that was going on, but he regretted that the -- the forensic unit was the only body included in this process, that no other bodies were included,; and that it was their tasks to obtain operative information that could be of assistance to this process in parallel with the procedure that was being led. From an operative point of view, how could they have obtained information? As I mentioned, this was done mainly by OVR Cair. People went on-site, people were called in for interviews; but, generally speaking, it was understood that the Albanian population from that area did not want to cooperate and generally blocked the work of the criminal police. They were called in, they promised to give information about persons and what happened; but later on, due to inexplicable circumstances which only they know, they withdrew immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I believe we have belaboured on this point, and we would like to avoid any repetitions. Could you please now look at the exhibit of the tab 32, which is Exhibit number P50.009. Before I ask you anything about this document, tell me, at the time when you had more frequent conversations with Mr. Stojanovski, did you also talk about a possible involvement of the judiciary in the events surrounding Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. He mentioned that, from day one, judicial bodies were also included, both investigative and the prosecution; that they're in constant communication. They ask certain information, and MOI submits information if they're able to do so. If they're blocked or unable to do so, they inform them why they're not able to provide such information. But from day one, they were informed about everything that was going on in the ministry, especially in particular to this case. If you allow me, can I ask, again, about the exhibit, the number of the exhibit you asked me to look at?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tab 32. You have the document on the screen as well. Were you able to find it?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've just told us that Mr. Stojanovski told you that when it came to this case, upon the requests of the court, if I understood you properly, it was mostly OVR Cair that replied to those requests because the event had actually taken place there. Did I understand you properly, or did he tell you something else with this regard?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: No. This is correct, that the response was given by OVR Cair.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the document and tell me whether you ever saw this document before, whether it was ever submitted to you, and whether you knew from these conversations that at the requests of the court and the prosecutors office who had already been involved with the case, did the police respond and reply to those requests?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. These are requests from the Basic Court. There were several such requests. They requested information, some data; and, of course, a reply was given to them in a timely fashion as requested.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please look at the document after tab 33. This is Exhibit P50.010. As you can see, Mrs. Galeva, this is another piece of information on the events and measures taken in the village of Ljuboten area from 10 August 2001 to 13 August 2001. Tell me, please, did you see this document before? Did you receive it from anybody; and if you did, can you tell us who it was you received it from?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. I know this document. I believe I received it in the material from Mr. Petre Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would kindly ask to you look at the another document. This time the document is after tab 34. The Exhibit number is P261. Do you have the document?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is an Official Note, number 537. This is a report on a deceased person. In the course of the performance of your duties, did you see this Official Note; and if you did, could you please tell us who gave it to you?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: The Official Note is known to me. I think it was also part of the materials received from Mr. Petre Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Galeva, at the beginning of your work, you were provided with the Human Rights Watch reports. Did you notice in those reports a reference made to a person who had died in hospital?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I noted there was a deviation from what is presented in the Human Rights Watch report and concretely in this Official Note for which there is proof. In their report, there is also an accusation that a person, Qaili Atulla, was brought in, beaten, as it is listed, to death, and that death occurred in a police, in the police station Mirkovci. However, the situation is altogether different. The above mentioned was kept in police station Mirkovci; but afterwards, urgent medical assistance was called in, and he was brought to the city hospital where a judge was also present. All of these bodies were immediately informed in order to enable them to be at the site, and then the Prosecutor took the work in his hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What you've just told us, Mrs. Galeva, I don't see it written in this note. Tell me, the information that you just shared with us, did you receive it from Mr. Stojanovski perhaps, when he provided you with this Official Note and when you asked him about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps Ms. Residovic could ask this important question in a less leading way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am trying very hard not to lead; but if this was leading, then obviously I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It certainly was leading, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've just told us about a situation. Tell me, how did you obtain the information that you have just shared with us?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: It was -- Mr. Petre Stojanovski told me this. I had this information in the material; and when he was explaining to me the matter at hand, I was also told all of this; and then I made a parallel, or, rather, I compared what was written in Human Rights Watch and what I was able to hear and read.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, in your conversations with Mr. Petre, did you also mention to whom this information was referred at the time, or did you not talk about that at all?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I cannot recall this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now I'm going to ask you to look at the document which is behind tab 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I think we better do that after the next break.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you kindly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We resume at five past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Galeva, you recall that, before the break, we viewed an Official Note dealing with the information related to the death of Atulla Qaili. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you now to look at the document in tab 3. That is Exhibit P46.16. Have you found this document?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the upper corner, we see who was the sender of this document. That is the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia, sector for internal affairs, Skopje, OVR-OOR Cair. The date is 14th of August, 2001. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you can see from the document that it was sent -- could you tell us who whom was it sent?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: To basic public prosecutor's office, Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could I ask you, please, to look at the attachment to the -- to this document. It is written there: "Attachment, experts testimony an analysis of fire-arm residue. Number 10.2.6-29836," and the second thing is Official Note number 537. You remember that this morning I showed you this document and that you stated you remembered having received some of the documents from the sector of security, Skopje. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, I recall this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the Official Note, number 237 [as interpreted], was attached this document, wasn't it? I will ask you to remain at this page and to look at the exhibit in tab 34. This is the Exhibit P261. Tell me, please, Mrs. Galeva, is this the actual document mentioned in the document of OVR Cair and that was forwarded to the basic public prosecutor's office, Skopje?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. This is the document, the Official Note number 537, which is attached to the document sent to the basic prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me also, Mrs. Galeva - if you know - what is the duty of the police when it learns about a death? Does it have any obligation to immediately inform anyone?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, always. In a case such as this, the police has the obligation to inform the duty public prosecutor. So it turns to the basic public prosecutor to inform him that a death has occurred of a person.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, then, who is in charge of all the obligations and the procedure once the police informs the public prosecutor or the investigating judge? Who then, if you were dealing with the criminal procedure; and if you know, who is in charge of the subsequent actions?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, once the police turns to the basic public prosecutor's office or to the investigating judge, at the same moment, the obligation of the police on that case ceases. Then there is a transfer of the obligations towards the judicial bodies, in this case to the public prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this clarification. Answering a previous question, you stated that among the materials that you received from the state security, if I understood you well, were included some analysis, a larger analysis report that contained information also from the operative department. Do you remember having said this answering to some of my questions this morning?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I think I mentioned that there was such a comprehensive analysis, but I did not present any details as far as I recall. I know I said there were numerous information by the bureau for security and counter-intelligence, but I don't recall having explained the details of this comprehensive analysis.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So do you know generally, considering your long years of experience in the ministry until the present day, what does the operative department deal with?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: This department is a unit part of the department for security and counter-intelligence, and its main activities are to follow persons, information, interception of telephone conversations. This is the operative aspect of this work. This was quite present and included in this comprehensive analysis done by the bureau for security, the UBK, which includes detailed information and data about concrete events.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, when you were gathering the materials, did you address this part of the MOI, asking them to provide you some information?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. I turned to the bureau for security and counter-intelligence, concretely, and at the first place with the director of this bureau. He gave me some materials which encompassed the whole period of the conflict, and he gave me materials which pertain to Ljuboten. Previously, I had received similar materials or the same materials also in that -- which I received from Mr. Goran Mitevski. These were materials from the operative unit, intercepts. I think I also mentioned that these were conversations of people brought in with their associates or collaborators or people which provided information, informants about the events. On the basis --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask the interpreters, maybe it has the same meaning, but the witness is speaking about the operative techniques, and we keep seeing "operational" instead of "operative" in the transcript. I'm not sure whether is that difference in the language. I would like to ask that it is stated as the witness is saying it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My apologies, Mrs. Galeva, because I saw that you used the same word twice and it was interpreted differently, and I'm not sure whether it is really proper. So please continue now. So you received this material from the director, it contained various information, and you wanted to add something now.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: In terms of the operative technicians, I think we wanted to speak a little bit more about this. As I mentioned, this is following persons, events, and interception of telephone conversations. It is interesting that this is all contained in the comprehensive information prepared by the UBK, which gives an overview of this whole approach and it focuses on Ljuboten which is very important. On the basis of this operative information and on the basis of the methods used by the operative technique, it was established that even before the event happened, this was planned. Even names are mentioned of some Albanians, who, at that time, were called commanders and who organised and coordinated this whole action, this whole thing. Furthermore, names of persons are mentioned from the village, from Ljuboten who provide logistic support in any way possible to these persons. Also mentioned is the manner of how this is to be done; some material resources, funds --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I was just interested to learn whether had you those materials as well. Perhaps it is not necessary to go into details unless my colleagues are interested in learning the findings you got there. I'm interested now, considering that you had conversations with everyone to worked in the MOI and who went to the SVR Skopje, and the events took place in the region covered by the SVR Cair, did you have any meetings or at least did you make efforts to meet with someone from that area?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Does this pertain concretely on the process of exhumation or about the whole materials that I was collecting?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am reminding of your task, to obtain all the information. So with the people directly related to the exhumation was one thing, but my question is dealing with your task as a whole, all the actions taken by the bodies in relation to the Ljuboten case.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Most of these meetings were individual meetings, I have to emphasise this, but I cannot exclude that there were a line of meetings. A number of meetings were held, where these problems discussed and where solutions for them were found. Would you want me to enumerate them?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We will go back to the question. My question before that was whether you had any communication with any individual from the OVR Cair. Did you go there, did anyone come to see, or did you or did you not have such communication?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: In view of the fact that on previous meetings that I had with Mr. Petre Stojanovski as the assistant of the criminal police and especially for the city of Skopje, he was in the best position to inform me what was happening with OVR Cair. He was in regular contact with the head of this OVR Cair, and this is the information I received from him. On several occasions, he emphasised that he regretted that the criminal police is, in effect, blocked to do its work due to many reasons; one being the lack of cooperation on the part of the Albanian villagers. As for getting information where the role of the police is being looked into to and its participation in all of these events, when I speak about the direct line of communication which he has with the head of OVR Cair, also he told me on several occasions that he is contact with them, that he is speaking with them, that a lot of efforts are being put into that end… they go out in the field, to the site, people are summoned, brought in and interviewed, but to no avail. However, the overall impression was that because nothing could be established was that this was a military operation that the police forces were later included once the operation was over.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You told me this already, but I wish to have a clear answer at the end of the line. Did you at any moment talk to the head of the OVR Cair and did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. I made an attempt to do so. I spoke on telephone with the head of OVR Cair, and I tried to set up a meeting with him. But even during on our telephone conversation, he categorically refused, because he said everything which he had to say was already said. All written material was submitted; therefore, there is nothing outside of this which he could add. And in addition, he asked me since, in effect, the Law on Amnesty had been passed for all persons which took part in the conflict, he asked me why are these efforts being made when everything seems to be resolved. He asked me about the goals of what I was doing, since, in effect, the Law on Amnesty had taken effect, why was this investigation taking place at all. This was my conversation with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mention some meetings. Tell us what sort of meetings were they and could you remember how many such meetings took place and who was present?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: There was an interesting meeting. First, I know, when I started dealing with this work, that there was a commission charged with working and drafting information about the Ljuboten event, the president of which was Director Goran Mitevski. However, one day, arriving in my office where I worked, I found a lot of people, including the external legal advisor Jordan Arsov, of the MOI, a former judge, who was following processes of these kinds, topical ongoing issues; and since they were already in my office and there were lots of people there, he presented them to me, and he told me that this was a working group, a commission, about war crimes. He presented to me the persons that were part of that commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you remember who were the persons present when you came to your office?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: As I already mentioned, advisor Jordan Arsov; the head of forensics, Miroslav Uslinkovski; then Apostol, for whom I later learned was the president of this commission, Apostol Stojanovski; then member of this commission, a certain Igno Stojkov, I believe was his last name; Atsanka [phoen], and I can't recall the last name; and a number of other persons. Arsov said that they were from the Prosecution; however, I cannot recall their names. There were several people from this body as well, and Mr. Mitevski, Director Goran Mitevski, was also present at this meet.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you were introduced to one another, tell me, were you able then -- so my first question is whether they were there alone, or did they have some documents, and did they tell what you was the nature of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: My first impression when I entered the office was the following: There was a large table stacked with documents, heaps of material, in front of everyone. They were all writing something, taking notes about this or that, and since I took -- I joined them somewhat later, during which time the presentation happened, which I mentioned about with Mr. Arsov and when he informed me what this commission was dealing with, that this commission was working on the basis of applications sent by inflicted, injured parties, Albanians and Macedonians, and that it collects information of -- about the Ljuboten case. They were here for a while, but it was a meeting that was probably at the end or maybe an informal gathering. I know that they agreed on some issues they were working on, which at that time I was not aware of, I was not informed of, and then we were dismissed. It was said that we now know each other; and if there is need, we would then further establish contacts between us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, was there any other time that you were invited and asked about the materials that you had collected in the fashion you described to the Chamber, collected from various bodies within the MOI?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I was called on several occasions by the director, Goran Mitevski, and by -- and by the minister. I was called in because the minister wanted to know literally how the procedure is going on, the material that was collected, the phase that we had reached.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At a given moment, were you asked to show the documents that you gathered; and if yes, when did this take place and whom did you show these documents to?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: This happened, first, by the director of the bureau for public security, Mr. Goran Mitevski, who called me in one day and told me to come with the material which I had collected, that I should come to his office. When I came there, he was present. There were public prosecutors; Stavre Dzikov; another Prosecutor, whose name escapes me; and another person who I believe was presented as a judge, but I really cannot recall their names; also the head of the criminal police, Spasen Sofevski. I came with the materials I had collected. Until then, it was in a register in a file in a chronological order. I recall that the public prosecutor of the Republic took the file and started going through it, started going through all the documents as they were listed, and he was looking at them with the people who were around them, either his deputies or judges or other assistants. They made some comments about this, and I remember that they agreed with the director that they talked about some documents. And as they were shifting through them, they would read what this document was about, and then they agreed or confirmed about that certain document; who they would meet with, when they would meet with a person, and so forth. They looked at it; they gave it back to me; and that until the next time they called me in, I should continue my work because it would be very useful if this material is enriched with additional documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you remember when did this meeting take place or roughly when?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: This happened, I cannot recall the exact date, but it was either the end of August or the beginning of September, around this time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After that meeting, when you showed the prosecutors the collection you managed to assemble, do you remember any other meeting related to the materials that you gathered from the moment that you were assigned to this duty until that time?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Other material?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Another meeting. Was there any other meeting where you were asked to bring the materials or to show them or to present it or whatever else, anything related to the materials?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Sometime after this meeting, there was also a meeting in the office of the minister; then I was told to go to the office and to bring the whole material. This was after some time. In this period of time, I collected additional materials. I enriched the file, and I was informed that this was at the request of the public prosecutor of the Republic, Mr. Stavre Dzikov. Again, the materials were listed in a chronological order of events, and I brought there material to the office of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was in the minister's office when you arrive there?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, the minister; two directors of the bureau for public security and the bureau for security and counter-intelligence; then the public prosecutor of the Republic. I cannot recall anyone else being there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you then requested to do something; and if yes, what was it?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I brought in the whole material that had been collected and established, and I recall that this material was taken by the public prosecutor general. He superficially looked at it to know what it contained, because there was also table of contents about what the material contains. I know that they spoke something with the minister and with the directors, that material has already been requested by the Tribunal, and that's why he is requesting this, which means that I understood this as being the goal, that this whole material should be given to him. At the same time, the minister charged me to make a copy of this material for him and for the other two directors, which I did after a few days.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, because I didn't understand well, was the entire collection of materials that you assembled handed over to the public prosecutor general?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. While I was there he looked at it and that's when -- that's how the conversation ended, that he should take it with him, that he should study it in more depth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mrs. Galeva, at the beginning you explained that there was a change of government, and that on the 1st of November you needed to leave your office because other persons came to work in the minister's cabinet. After you handed over those materials to the public prosecutor general and gave copies to the directors of the state and of public security, until the date when you left the office, did you hear any comment from anyone or any information related to the issues that you gathered information in relation to; namely, the issue of responsibility of the minister, who was in the village, who ordered the action, or anything that was the subject of your interest when you gathered the materials?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you make the question a little more concrete? Do you mean about information from the ministry or outside the ministry which I had heard?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that, on the 1st of November, you left your office. I'm interested to learn whether any of your former superiors, any director, minister, or anyone else, before you left the office, gave you any information pertaining to your work.

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I left my office on the 1st of November, 2002; although, as I had clarified earlier, I remained on that position until 2003, but I was told to leave and I had to leave my office. With the coming of the new minister, many new transfers were made, many employees were deployed on different work positions, and so forth. What I can recall is that immediately prior to my departure, November it was, 2002, I met with the director of the bureau for public security, Goran Mitevski, who was already outgoing. And in a short conversation with him, he mentioned and he gave me a very interesting information, which he said, at any cost, he would leave the ministry but not until he fulfilled one important obligation. That means that he received such an obligation from the minister. The ministry gave him a certain piece of information prepared by the Ministry of Defence, by Mr. Buckovski, information that could really help establish any issues, dilemmas; can help provide the answers to many questions which until then had been very difficult to obtain; that the epilogue of this whole information speaks loads about the fact that there is no responsibility of the police forces as participants in this event; and that it is, above all, a military operation. It was even mentioned -- an order of the president of the Republic was even mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So my final question: Have you ever seen this information that the Director Mitevski mentioned to you?

utterances.speaker: SOFIJA GALEVA-PETROVSKA
utterances.text: I personally have not seen this. This was a short conversation. He just clarified how he obtained this information and what his task was, that prior to his leaving he should give this over to the new minister or to the new director of the bureau for public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mrs. Galeva, for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this concludes my examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well timed, Ms. Residovic. Thank you for that. We, of course, must now adjourn. It's just on a quarter to 2.00. We resume tomorrow at 9.00. My I ask you to return tomorrow morning to continue the questioning. The evidence will continue at 9.00 in the morning, and there will be questions by other counsel at that time. We adjourn now, to resume tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 1st day of February, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.
